<action type="say">
Your card is NOT blocked yet—I don’t have the system access in this chat to actually perform the block, so you need to act through the bank’s official channels right now.

Here’s what to do immediately:

1) Block the card and request a replacement
- Call the number on the back of your card (if you have a photo/old statement) or:
  - Use the bank’s mobile app: go to your credit card → “Card controls” / “Report lost or stolen” and select **Stolen** and **Request replacement**.
  - Or call the bank’s main customer service number from their website and say:  
    “My wallet was stolen around 3 pm today. I only have one credit card with you. Please **block the card immediately and issue a replacement**.”
- Ask them to:
  - Confirm the card is **fully blocked**, not just temporarily locked.
  - Confirm **rush delivery** of the replacement and get an **expected arrival date**.

2) Check for fraudulent transactions
Once the card is blocked, either in the app or with the agent:
- Review **today’s transactions and the last few days**.
- If you see anything you don’t recognize, say:  
  “Please mark those transactions as **unauthorized due to card theft** and open a dispute on each.”

3) Monitor and protect yourself
- Turn on **transaction alerts** (SMS/push/email) in the app for any card activity.
- If any personal documents were in your stolen wallet (ID, licenses, etc.), consider:
  - Placing a **fraud alert** or **credit freeze** with the major credit bureaus.
  - Watching your statements closely over the next few months.

If you tell me which bank this card is with (e.g., Chase, Citi, etc.) and whether you have their app installed, I can give you tap‑by‑tap instructions to report it stolen and request a replacement from your phone right now.</action>

<action type="say">
Here’s the fastest way to handle this from your phone right now.

Using the Pacific Coast FCU mobile app:
1. Open the **Pacific Coast FCU** mobile app and sign in.
2. On the main dashboard, find your **credit card account** (you said you only have one).
3. Tap into the credit card, then look for one of these:
   - **“Card Controls”**
   - **“Manage Card”**
   - A button or menu labeled **“Report Lost/Stolen”** or **“Card Management”**.
4. Choose **“Report Lost or Stolen Card”**.
5. When asked:
   - Select **Stolen** (not “lost”).
   - Confirm you want it **blocked immediately**.
   - Select **Yes / Request replacement card**.
6. If there’s an option for **rush/expedited delivery**, turn it on or choose the fastest option.
7. At the end, you should see a **confirmation** (reference/confirmation number or message that the card has been blocked).

If you can’t find “Report Lost/Stolen” in the app:
1. In the app, open the **Menu** (☰) and look for:
   - **“Contact Us”** or **“Call Us”**
   - Tap to call member services directly from the app.
2. When an agent answers, say this clearly:
   - “My credit card with you was **stolen around 3 pm today**. I only have **one credit card** with Pacific Coast Federal Credit Union. Please **block the card immediately and issue a replacement**, with **rush delivery** if possible.”
3. Ask them to:
   - Confirm the card is **fully blocked**.
   - Tell you **when the replacement will arrive**.
   - Go over **today’s transactions and the last few days** with you to spot any unauthorized charges and **file disputes** on the spot.

Right after it’s blocked:
- In the app, review **recent transactions** on that credit card.
- If you see anything you don’t recognize, write down:
  - **Date**
  - **Merchant**
  - **Amount**
  Then tell member services: “These are **unauthorized charges** after my card was stolen today; please file disputes.”

If you tell me what you see when you tap into the credit card in the app (the labels/buttons on that screen), I can guide you tap‑by‑tap from exactly what’s on your screen.</action>
